section: Issues and challenges in Indian federalism - governor's role, GST Council, central agencies, All India Services
subsections: Commissions on Centre-State relations - year, chairman, appointing government, odd one out
Commission recommendations - Inter-State Council, Article 356, All India Services, Governor

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Body — Chairman
1. Administrative Reforms Commission — Morarji Desai
2. Rajamannar Committee — Dr P.V. Rajamannar
3. Sarkaria Commission — Justice R.S. Sarkaria
4. Punchhi Commission — Justice M.M. Punchhi
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Morarji Desai initially chaired the ARC, while Dr P.V. Rajamannar, Justice R.S. Sarkaria and Justice M.M. Punchhi chaired the respective committees or commissions.
accepted.tq: Use direct chairman-name matching and verify all pairs before selecting the comprehensive option.
accepted.sec: Commissions on Centre-State relations - year, chairman, appointing government, odd one out  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Administrative Reforms Commission on Centre-State relations was appointed by the Union Government in which year?
accepted.x: The Administrative Reforms Commission was appointed by the Centre in 1966. Its study team report was submitted in 1969.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the year of constitution from the later year of the study-team report.
accepted.sec: Commissions on Centre-State relations - year, chairman, appointing government, odd one out  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Who headed the study team of the Administrative Reforms Commission dealing with Centre-State relations?
accepted.x: M.C. Setalvad headed the ARC study team. Morarji Desai and later K. Hanumanthaiya were associated with the broader Administrative Reforms Commission.
accepted.tq: Separate the chairman of the main commission from the head of its study team.
accepted.sec: Commissions on Centre-State relations - year, chairman, appointing government, odd one out  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was the first State-level review of Centre-State relations?
accepted.x: The Rajamannar Committee, appointed by the Tamil Nadu Government, was the first State-level review of Centre-State relations. Its report was submitted in 1971 after its constitution in 1969.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive description rather than relying only on the year.
accepted.sec: Commissions on Centre-State relations - year, chairman, appointing government, odd one out  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Rajamannar Committee:
1. It was appointed by the Tamil Nadu Government.
2. It consisted of three members.
3. Its recommendations were accepted by the Union Government.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Centre ignored the Rajamannar Committee's recommendations, so statement 3 is incorrect.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the Centre's response to a State-level committee.
accepted.sec: Commissions on Centre-State relations - year, chairman, appointing government, odd one out  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following bodies in chronological order of their appointment or constitution:
A. Punchhi Commission
B. Rajamannar Committee
C. Sarkaria Commission
D. NCRWC
accepted.x: The Rajamannar Committee was constituted in 1969, the Sarkaria Commission in 1983, the NCRWC in 2000 and the Punchhi Commission in 2007.
accepted.tq: Fix the earliest and latest bodies first, then place the two intervening commissions.
accepted.sec: Commissions on Centre-State relations - year, chairman, appointing government, odd one out  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following recommendations was made by the Administrative Reforms Commission regarding Centre-State relations?
o: Creation of an All India Judicial Service
A permanent Inter-State Council under Article 263
Non-partisan Governors and greater delegation and finances to States
accepted.x: The ARC recommended non-partisan Governors and greater delegation of powers and finances to the States. Complete abolition of Article 356 was associated with the Rajamannar Committee, while an All India Judicial Service was recommended by the NCRWC.
accepted.tq: Match each recommendation with the correct commission instead of the neighbouring commission.
accepted.sec: Commission recommendations - Inter-State Council, Article 356, All India Services, Governor  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was a recommendation of the Rajamannar Committee?
o: Appointment of Governors as recent active politicians
A four-month period for assent to every Bill
Strengthening of the All India Services
accepted.x: The Rajamannar Committee recommended abolishing the Planning Commission, eliminating Article 356 and establishing an Inter-State Council under Article 263.
accepted.tq: Use the commission-specific recommendation and reject proposals belonging to other bodies.
accepted.sec: Commission recommendations - Inter-State Council, Article 356, All India Services, Governor  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to the Sarkaria Commission, consider the following statements:
1. It favoured a permanent Inter-State Council.
2. It recommended that Article 356 should be used very sparingly and as a last resort.
3. It favoured abolishing the All India Services.
4. It recommended consultation with States on laws relating to the Concurrent List.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct. The Sarkaria Commission favoured strengthening the All India Services, not abolishing them, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed recommendation concerning All India Services.
accepted.sec: Commission recommendations - Inter-State Council, Article 356, All India Services, Governor  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was recommended by the National Commission to Review the Working of the Constitution regarding the Governor's handling of Bills?
o: The Governor should decide Bills only after a referendum
Every Bill should be reserved for the President
Assent should be withheld indefinitely in case of disagreement with the State Cabinet
Assent should be given within about four months
accepted.x: The NCRWC recommended that assent to Bills should be given within about four months. It also suggested safeguards concerning Article 356 and an order of preference in a hung Assembly.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise time-bound recommendation and reject extreme alternatives.
accepted.sec: Commission recommendations - Inter-State Council, Article 356, All India Services, Governor  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a recommendation associated with the Punchhi Commission?
o: Fixed tenure for Governors and no misuse of discretionary powers
accepted.x: The Punchhi Commission recommended a fixed tenure for Governors, no misuse of discretion, a President-like removal procedure, time-bound disposal of Bills and regular Prime Minister–Chief Minister meetings.
accepted.tq: Distinguish Punchhi's Governor-related recommendations from the more radical Rajamannar proposals.
accepted.sec: Commission recommendations - Inter-State Council, Article 356, All India Services, Governor  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The 11th meeting of the Inter-State Council was held on:
accepted.x: The 11th meeting of the Inter-State Council was held on 16 July 2016.
accepted.tq: Recall the exact day, month and year rather than inferring a recent meeting date.
accepted.sec: Commission recommendations - Inter-State Council, Article 356, All India Services, Governor  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Under Article 312, which of the following services are All India Services?
o: IAS, Indian Foreign Service and Indian Forest Service
IPS, IFS and Indian Audit and Accounts Service
IAS, IPS and Indian Forest Service
IAS, IRS and Indian Revenue Service
accepted.x: The All India Services referred to under Article 312 are the Indian Administrative Service, Indian Police Service and Indian Forest Service.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the Indian Forest Service from similarly abbreviated or centrally recruited services.
accepted.sec: Offices and services said to violate the federal principle - All India Services  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A new All India Service can be created only when the Rajya Sabha passes a resolution supported by:
o: A unanimous vote of all State representatives
Two-thirds of the members present and voting
A simple majority of the total membership
accepted.x: Article 312 requires a Rajya Sabha resolution supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting for creation of a new All India Service.
accepted.tq: Separate the constitutional voting threshold from the different concept of two-thirds of total membership.
accepted.sec: Offices and services said to violate the federal principle - All India Services  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best describes the control structure of All India Service officers?
o: Ultimate control rests with the Centre and immediate control with the States
Ultimate control rests with the States and immediate control with the Centre
Both ultimate and immediate control rest exclusively with the Centre
Both levels of control rest exclusively with local governments
accepted.x: All India Service officers serve the States under immediate State control, while ultimate control rests with the Centre. Their uniform pay scales operate across States.
accepted.tq: Compare ultimate and immediate control instead of treating administrative control as belonging to one level alone.
accepted.sec: Offices and services said to violate the federal principle - All India Services  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following explains why All India Services are viewed as restricting State autonomy?
1. Officers are governed in important respects by Central rules.
2. States cannot fully discipline or remove such officers.
3. Officers are recruited by the Union Public Service Commission but serve in the States.
4. All India Services have no role in Centre-State coordination.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct and explain the perceived restriction on State autonomy. Statement 4 is false because All India Services are also defended as promoting Centre-State coordination.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute negative statement and connect recruitment, rules and disciplinary control.
accepted.sec: Offices and services said to violate the federal principle - All India Services  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is a justification offered in support of All India Services?
o: They ensure that all officers are controlled only by State governments
They eliminate all State-level administrative discretion
They remove the need for constitutional division of powers
They promote high standards, uniformity and Centre-State coordination
accepted.x: All India Services are defended on the grounds that they maintain high standards, promote uniformity and facilitate Centre-State coordination.
accepted.tq: Identify the stated functional justification rather than the criticism based on State autonomy.
accepted.sec: Offices and services said to violate the federal principle - All India Services  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. Rajamannar Committee — Tamil Nadu
2. Anandpur Sahib Resolution — Punjab
3. West Bengal memorandum — West Bengal
4. Kerala autonomy demand — Kerala
accepted.x: The Rajamannar Committee, Anandpur Sahib Resolution and West Bengal memorandum are correctly associated with Tamil Nadu, Punjab and West Bengal respectively. Kerala is the odd one out because it had no formal autonomy demand in this context.
accepted.tq: Use the odd-one-out pair to test whether a State actually made a formal autonomy demand.
accepted.sec: State autonomy demands - which state  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution was associated with which political party and year?
accepted.x: The Anandpur Sahib Resolution was associated with the Akali Dal in Punjab and was adopted in 1973.
accepted.tq: Match the political party and year with the correct State autonomy document.
accepted.sec: State autonomy demands - which state  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The West Bengal memorandum on Centre-State relations was submitted under which government?
accepted.x: The West Bengal memorandum was associated with the Left Front government and was issued in 1977.
accepted.tq: Pair the document with the State government that presented it.
accepted.sec: State autonomy demands - which state  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Which of the following demands was associated with the Tamil Nadu autonomy position?
1. Deletion of Article 356
2. Abolition of the All India Services
3. Abolition of the Planning Commission
4. Restriction of the Centre to defence, foreign affairs, currency and communications only
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Tamil Nadu's autonomy position included deletion of Article 356, abolition of the All India Services and abolition of the Planning Commission. Restriction of the Centre to four subjects was specifically associated with Punjab and West Bengal.
accepted.tq: Separate the Tamil Nadu-specific demands from the common four-subject demand of Punjab and West Bengal.
accepted.sec: State autonomy demands - which state  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Punjab and West Bengal demanded that the Union Government should principally confine itself to which of the following subjects?
o: Industry, labour, taxation and social welfare
Agriculture, education, health and local government
Defence, foreign affairs, communications and currency
accepted.x: Punjab and West Bengal wanted the Centre to be confined to defence, foreign affairs, communications and currency.
accepted.tq: Recall the four-subject formulation and watch for substitution by State List subjects.
accepted.sec: State autonomy demands - which state  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the major themes of State autonomy demands in India?
o: More powers for States, greater own revenue and reduced central administrative control
Uniform language policy imposed by all State governments
Transfer of defence and foreign affairs exclusively to local bodies
Complete abolition of State legislatures and concentration of taxation in the Centre
accepted.x: State autonomy demands generally sought more powers, greater control over own revenue, less central administrative control and protection of linguistic interests.
accepted.tq: Choose the option that combines the recurring federal, financial, administrative and linguistic dimensions.
accepted.sec: State autonomy demands - which state  [APPSC]
